headers.Glyphh-Contract: On every answer of the Ada host: the contract it speaks (5). A client that speaks an older one fails, asking to be upgraded, rather than read shapes it does not know
headers.Glyphh-Ada: On every answer about one model (its info, versions, decide and every read): the Ada version its active version runs, e.g. ada-1-0
headers.Glyphh-Ada-Notice: When the model runs a deprecated Ada version, or was just moved off a retired one: `<kind>: <message>`, kind deprecated or moved. The SDKs warn with it

ada_versions.title: AdaVersions
ada_versions.description: GET /v1/ada: every Ada version the cloud lists, newest first, with the latest stable (the default for a new model, an upgrade and a backtest's target) and the contract the server speaks. A customer sees names (ada-<major>-<minor>, -beta for a beta); the kernel's semver only in a release's details. status: stable or beta, then deprecated (still answering, until ends), then retired (its models moved to the latest stable). A beta is never the default and is chosen only by name; open false closes it to new models. changes_answers: against the version before it. models: how many of the org's models run it

model.title: Model
model.description: GET /v1/models/{name} (and what POST /v1/models {name, spec, ada?} answers, the model made, version 1 on the Ada asked for, else the latest stable): the model, its active version and spec, how many precedents it holds, and the Ada version that version runs. ada_status is that version's status; ada_notice what to tell the person: upgrade (a newer stable exists: to), beta (a beta is open to try: to, the quiet one), deprecated (its version ends: to, ends), moved (it was moved off a retired one: to), retired; null when there is nothing to say (a model on the beta itself says so by ada_status)

models.title: Models
models.description: GET /v1/models: the org's models, each with its active version, its precedents and the Ada version it runs

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: GET /v1/models/{name}/versions: every version, oldest first: who made it, when and why, which is active, and the Ada version it was made and learned with (ada, the name chosen; kernel, the exact release). A new version from a spec or settings change keeps its model's Ada; only an upgrade changes it. Rollback to a version on another Ada (POST .../versions/{n}/activate) answers on that version's Ada

upgrade.title: Upgrade
upgrade.description: POST /v1/models/{name}/upgrade {ada?, note?, backtest?} (no ada: the latest stable; any supported version, an older one too, a downgrade): a new version of the active spec on that Ada, always re-encoded by a job on its kernel while the old version serves; when the job is done the new version is active. from: the Ada it ran. The same Ada: 409 E_NO_CHANGE. Rollback: POST .../versions/{n}/activate

backtest.title: Backtest
backtest.description: A done backtest job's result (POST /v1/models/{name}/backtest {candidates?, holdout?, output?, clearance?, ada?}): the active version and each candidate scored on the same held-out precedents, each learned on the rest by its own Ada's kernel. A candidate may name an Ada ({"ada": "ada-1-1-beta"} alone, the active spec on that Ada, or with settings, spec_version or spec); a body's ada is shorthand for that candidate. ada on the active run and on each candidate says which scored it; change is each candidate against the active

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: What POST /v1/decide answers: the outcome of least expected cost under the spec's costs, the calibrated probabilities, whether a person should decide instead (ask: the outcome is then the best guess), the precedents it stands on, and the model, active version and Ada version that answered. include: ["facts"] adds the nearest fact tree; outputs: [...] answers {outputs: {name: decided}, model, version, ada} instead

job.title: Job
job.description: Work too long for a request, from GET /v1/jobs/{id} and every call that starts one (learn, calibrate, imports, export, backtest; a spec or settings change, or an activation, that re-encodes answers one as its job): its state and percent, then its result or error. A done export carries download {url, expires_at}; an import waiting for its file, upload {url, expires_at}: one-hour signed links, each its own credential

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: GET /v1/usage (the same object is `cloud` on the account API's /v1/me and /v1/billing): the org's plan, the calendar month counted (UTC) and the day it starts again, its live models, the precedents they hold against the plan's, its requests this month against the plan's (reads: decide, query, probabilities, facts; a decide of several outputs once per output; `over`: past the month, metered on Basic, Pro and Team; `overage` false: refused past it, E_LIMIT requests), and the plan's calls a second. A null max is by contract: no cap

ada.description: Contract 5: the org's Ada versions, as GET /v1/ada answers them (latest_stable, contract, versions with the org's models on each)

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: What an Ada model's query answers: POST /v1/models/{name}/query, and data of a done Result of query

result.title: Result
result.description: SDK 3.0's call shape: what POST /v1/runs {model, function, inputs, clearance?} answers. Ada Cloud answers record, query, facts, probabilities, decide, learn and settings at once, done, the function's answer as data

error.title: Error
error.description: Every refusal: a stable code to branch on, a message for people, the trace id to quote to support, and the refusal's own detail beside them (E_LIMIT precedents: reason, used, max, adding; E_LIMIT requests, 403, the month's reads used on a plan that is not metered: reason, used, max, plan, upgrade (the self-serve plan that reads more, null: talk to sales), resets_at (YYYY-MM-DD); E_RATE, 429, past the plan's calls a second: reason, max, retry_after, and the Retry-After header; E_SPEC: path; E_SPEC_LIMIT: limit, max; E_SPEC_READING: roles; E_BUSY: job, kind; E_INVALID: problems or reason; the Ada version refusals, E_ADA_UNKNOWN 422, E_ADA_RETIRED 410, E_ADA_DEPRECATED 422 (chosen for a new model or as an upgrade target), E_ADA_BETA 422 (a beta closed to new models), E_ADA_UNAVAILABLE 503 (a kernel this deploy does not have, not retried): ada, the name asked for, and latest, the latest stable, named as the fix; E_NO_CHANGE 409 from an upgrade to the Ada the model runs). A 429 or 503 may carry Retry-After
